high_level_overview.overview: COTRN01C is part of the CardDemo application, a credit card management system that handles transaction processing and account management. This program operates within the transaction inquiry workflow, allowing authorized users to look up and view detailed information about individual credit card transactions. The program serves as a read-only transaction viewer, enabling customer service or back-office staff to retrieve and display full transaction details from the TRANSACT file by entering a transaction ID, supporting research, dispute resolution, and audit activities.

key_features.description: Retrieves a specific transaction record from the TRANSACT file using a user-supplied transaction ID as the key.
Presents comprehensive transaction information including transaction ID, card number, type, category, source, amount, description, origination/processing timestamps, and merchant details.
Validates that the transaction ID field is not empty before attempting a file read, providing a clear error message if the field is blank.
Handles file read errors including 'not found' and unexpected CICS response codes, displaying appropriate messages to the user.
Supports PF3 to return to the calling program, PF4 to clear the current screen, and PF5 to navigate to the transaction list screen (COTRN00C).
Accepts a pre-selected transaction ID passed via the communication area from a prior screen, automatically performing the lookup on first entry.
Populates the screen header with current date, time, program name, and transaction ID on every screen send for consistent user orientation.
Maintains session state and navigation context across screen interactions using a shared COMMAREA, enabling seamless program-to-program transitions.

input_output.name: TRANSACT
input_output.description: Transaction file - reads a single transaction record by Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) to retrieve and display transaction details including card number, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant info, and timestamps

data_flow.description: Program checks EIBCALEN to determine if a communication area exists. If zero, redirects to sign-on screen COSGN00C. Otherwise, copies DFHCOMMAREA into CARDDEMO-COMMAREA for processing.

On first entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER not set), sets re-entry flag, clears output map COTRN1AO, and checks if a transaction was pre-selected via CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SELECTED. If pre-selected, copies it to TRNIDINI and triggers PROCESS-ENTER-KEY automatically.
On re-entry, receives the BMS map COTRN1A from mapset COTRN01 into COTRN1AI, capturing the transaction ID entered by the user. Response codes are stored in WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD.

Evaluates EIBAID to determine user action: ENTER triggers transaction lookup, PF3 returns to previous or default menu screen, PF4 clears the screen, PF5 navigates to transaction list screen COTRN00C. Invalid keys set error flag and redisplay screen.

Validates that TRNIDINI is not spaces or low-values. If empty, sets error flag, populates error message, sets cursor to transaction ID field, and sends screen. If valid, clears all display fields and moves TRNIDINI to TRAN-ID for file read.

data_flow.process: Read Transaction Record from TRANSACT File
data_flow.description: Issues a CICS READ with UPDATE against the TRANSACT dataset using TRAN-ID as the key. Reads the full TRAN-RECORD into working storage. Handles NOTFND and OTHER error conditions by setting error flag and displaying appropriate messages.

If no error, maps all transaction record fields to the output map COTRN1AI. Formats TRAN-AMT through WS-TRAN-AMT for display. Fields populated include transaction ID, card number, type code, category code, source, amount, description, timestamps, and merchant details.

Retrieves current date and time using FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE. Formats and moves date components (MM, DD, YY) and time components (HH, MM, SS) to screen header fields. Also moves screen titles, transaction ID, and program name to header output fields.
Sends the populated BMS map COTRN1A from mapset COTRN01 to the terminal using ERASE and CURSOR options. Error message from WS-MESSAGE is moved to ERRMSGO before sending.

data_flow.process: Return to CICS with Transaction ID
data_flow.description: Issues CICS RETURN with transaction ID CT01 and the updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, keeping the pseudo-conversational session alive for the next user interaction.

When navigation keys (PF3, PF5) are pressed, sets CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM in COMMAREA, then issues CICS XCTL to transfer control to the target program (COMEN01C, COTRN00C, or COSGN00C).

data_dependencies.description: The program cannot function without a valid COMMAREA (EIBCALEN > 0). If absent, the user is immediately redirected to the sign-on screen, preventing any transaction lookup.

The program's behavior on entry is entirely controlled by the CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag in COMMAREA. First entry triggers initialization and optional auto-lookup; subsequent entries trigger screen receive and AID processing.

CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SELECTED in COMMAREA may be populated by a calling program (e.g., transaction list screen). If set, the program automatically performs a transaction lookup without waiting for user input, creating a dependency on the calling program's data.

data_dependencies.dependency: TRAN-ID Must Exist in TRANSACT File
data_dependencies.description: The READ-TRANSACT-FILE paragraph depends on TRAN-ID matching an existing record in the TRANSACT VSAM dataset. A NOTFND response halts display and shows an error, making the entire screen population dependent on file record existence.

data_dependencies.dependency: TRANSACT File Opened with UPDATE Intent
data_dependencies.description: The CICS READ is issued with the UPDATE option, which acquires a record-level lock on the transaction record. This lock is held until the task ends or a REWRITE/UNLOCK is issued, potentially blocking concurrent updates to the same transaction record by other tasks.

All downstream processing after validation and file read is gated on ERR-FLG-OFF. If any prior step sets WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y', screen field population is skipped entirely, creating a strict sequential dependency between validation, file I/O, and display steps.

The PF3 return navigation depends on CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM being populated in COMMAREA by the calling program. If absent or spaces, the program defaults to COMEN01C, making correct back-navigation dependent on the calling program setting this field.

Screen input and output depend on COTRN01 copybook defining COTRN1AI and COTRN1AO map structures correctly. Any mismatch between the BMS mapset definition and the copybook would cause incorrect field mapping for all transaction display fields.

data_dependencies.dependency: CVTRA05Y Record Layout Alignment with TRANSACT File
data_dependencies.description: The READ-TRANSACT-FILE paragraph reads directly into TRAN-RECORD as defined by CVTRA05Y. The physical VSAM record layout must exactly match this copybook structure for all field extractions (TRAN-AMT, TRAN-CARD-NUM, etc.) to be correct.

external_system_integrations.purpose: Manages the entire pseudo-conversational execution lifecycle including SEND/RECEIVE of BMS maps for terminal I/O, READ of the TRANSACT VSAM dataset, XCTL for program-to-program control transfer, and RETURN to maintain the conversational state across user interactions.

Handles formatted screen presentation and input collection using mapset COTRN01 and map COTRN1A. BMS manages field-level attributes, cursor positioning, and data transfer between the 3270 terminal and the application program.

Stores transaction records keyed by TRAN-ID. The program reads individual transaction records by key to display full transaction details including amount, card number, merchant information, and processing timestamps.

called_programs.name: COSGN00C.cbl
called_programs.purpose: COSGN00C is the entry point for the CardDemo application, a credit card management system running on IBM mainframe under CICS. It serves as the security gateway that controls access to all downstream application functions, operating as the first screen users encounter when initiating the CC00 transaction. The program presents a signon screen to collect user credentials, validates them against a security file, and routes authenticated users to the appropriate menu based on their user type — either an administrative dashboard or a standard customer menu — effectively enforcing role-based access control for the entire application.

error_handling.description: Validates that the Transaction ID field is not empty or low-values before attempting a file read. When invalid, sets WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y', populates WS-MESSAGE with a descriptive message ('Tran ID can NOT be empty...'), positions the cursor on the offending field via TRNIDINL=-1, and redisplays the screen. Subsequent processing is gated by checking ERR-FLG-ON, preventing file reads when validation fails.

After the CICS READ against the TRANSACT dataset, the RESP code is evaluated using DFHRESP conditions. NOTFND produces a user-friendly message ('Transaction ID NOT found...') with cursor repositioning and screen redisplay. Any other non-normal response triggers a DISPLAY of raw RESP/REAS codes to the system log for diagnostics, sets the error flag, shows 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' to the user, and redisplays the screen. Normal response allows processing to continue silently.

If EIBCALEN=0 (no commarea, unexpected entry point), the program immediately redirects to the sign-on program COSGN00C via RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN rather than attempting to process. If CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is spaces or low-values during navigation, it defaults to COSGN00C as a safe fallback destination.

Unrecognized AID keys (anything other than ENTER, PF3, PF4, PF5) are caught in the WHEN OTHER branch of the EIBAID EVALUATE. The error flag is set to 'Y' and the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY from the CSMSG01Y copybook) is moved to WS-MESSAGE and displayed on screen, with no further processing attempted.

A single WS-ERR-FLG ('Y'/'N') with 88-level conditions (ERR-FLG-ON/ERR-FLG-OFF) acts as a global error gate throughout the program. Once set, it prevents downstream processing blocks (file reads, data population) from executing via IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON guards. The flag is reset to 'N' at the start of each MAIN-PARA invocation, ensuring clean state per transaction cycle.

The RECEIVE-TRNVIEW-SCREEN paragraph captures RESP and REAS codes into WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD, but does not explicitly evaluate them after the CICS RECEIVE. No error branching is implemented for map receive failures, representing a gap in error handling for BMS receive anomalies.

overview.business_function: Provides a read-only view interface for displaying detailed transaction information from the TRANSACT file. Users enter a Transaction ID to retrieve and display all associated transaction details including card number, type, category, source, amount, dates, description, and merchant information.
